citations.title: Home Health, Home Services, and Home Nursing Agency Licensing Act
citations.requirement: No one may open, manage, conduct or maintain a home services agency without an IDPH license. The Act is the enabling statute for 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245. (From the fact-checked research; Act text not re-fetched.)

citations.title: Home Health, Home Services, and Home Nursing Agency Code
citations.requirement: Part 245 has four subparts: A General (245.10-245.25), B Operational Requirements (245.30-245.75), C Licensure Procedures (245.80-245.150), D Client/Patient Services (245.200-245.250). Section titles were confirmed from the table of contents. Most recent amendment shown: 49 Ill. Reg. 4661, eff. 3/25/2025.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Programs serving clients exclusively through IDoA CCP, DHS Office of Rehabilitation Services, or the VA are not home services agencies. 'Client record' means personal information, emergency notification information, agreed service plans, the home services contract, and documentation of services at each visit.

citations.title: Organization and Administration - Governing Body (all agencies)
citations.requirement: The agency must have a governing body with legal authority. The body must have bylaws or the equivalent, reviewed annually and revised as needed, that state the agency's objectives. It must adopt and revise operating policies and procedures, meet to review agency operations, and keep minutes of all meetings. The requirement to employ a qualified administrator is for home health agencies.

citations.title: Administration - all agencies
citations.requirement: The agency needs written administrative policies and procedures to ensure safe and adequate care. It must show evidence of liability insurance per 245.90(a). It must have written complaint-resolution policies between the agency and its clients and client advocates.

citations.title: Personnel policies - all agencies
citations.requirement: Written personnel policies must cover: (A) wage scales, benefits, hours and leave; (B) initial health evaluation of each new employee with client contact; (C) orientation and continuing education; (D) job descriptions for all positions; (E) annual performance evaluation; (F) Civil Rights Act of 1964 compliance; (G) confidentiality of personnel records; (H) employee health policy, including symptom and exposure reporting and removal from and return to client contact; (I) procedures for identifying and protecting staff from dangers in the home.

citations.title: Personnel - license verification, personnel records, contracted staff
citations.requirement: Before employing anyone in a position needing a State professional license, verify with IDFPR that the license is active and keep a copy in the personnel file. Personnel records must hold name and address, SSN, date of birth, next of kin, evidence of qualifications, employment dates, and the reason for separation. Home services agencies that use contracted services must ensure those workers hold any required license, registration or certification and are supervised by the agency.

citations.title: Agency Manager - Home Services and Home Nursing Agencies
citations.requirement: A home services agency must designate a person to supervise the provision of services (or oversee placement of workers). This is the verified designation rule. The research's reference to '245.40(f)' could not be confirmed and should not be used. No manager qualification list for home services agencies appears in 245.30(f) as fetched.

citations.title: Staffing - Administrator or Agency Manager responsibilities
citations.requirement: The manager must ensure legal compliance, know the Department's rules, keep them in the agency, and familiarize employees with the Act and rules. The manager keeps reports, records, personnel files and policies, maintains an organizational chart, hires per job descriptions, and provides orientation and in-service education. The manager must designate in writing a qualified person to act in the manager's absence. The agency must keep an office with a working telephone staffed during business hours. The office must protect record confidentiality and comply with fire-safety ordinances. The agency must adopt a written operating-hours policy that tells clients how to access care outside those hours.

citations.title: Home Services or In-Home Services Worker - definition and duties
citations.requirement: Home services means help with ADLs, housekeeping, personal laundry and companionship in the client's residence. It excludes anything requiring a Nurse Practice Act licensee. Workers may observe and report changes in client functioning, do chores and meal preparation, help with shopping and appointments, provide companionship, document services, and assist with ADLs and personal care. Workers provide services only as Part 245 allows.

citations.title: Acceptable tasks and limitations (skin care through toileting)
citations.requirement: Task-by-task limits apply for skin care, ambulation, bathing, dressing/compression, exercise, feeding/thickener, hair care, mouth care, nail care, positioning, shaving and toileting. Most require three things: client or representative feedback, worker training in the method, and an agency competency evaluation. Several also require a health care professional's order. No passive range of motion, no nail trimming, and no skilled skin care. The fetched page was truncated after toileting (L), so the remaining items (M-P) must be read in full.

citations.title: Medication reminding; prohibited medication setup
citations.requirement: A worker may remind a client about medications only when they were pre-selected by the client, a family member, a nurse or a pharmacist and are in containers other than prescription bottles, such as medication minders. A worker may not perform or provide medication setup. Source: ilga.gov excerpts and the Illinois Register adoption text, seen in search results. Confirm the exact subsection wording in the full text.

citations.title: Supervision of a home services worker
citations.requirement: A supervisor must be designated and available to workers for questions at all times (not applicable to placement agencies). Supervisory visits must include an on-site visit within the next supervisory visit when an area of concern is noted. The supervisor must also make an annual on-site visit to observe and assess each worker giving care. The visit interval for routine supervision is not confirmed. A secondary source says 90 days; read the full text of (c)(6)(B) before publishing.

citations.title: Qualifications and Requirements for Home Services Workers - employment conditions
citations.requirement: For each worker who is not otherwise licensed, certified or registered, the agency must keep in the employee file documentation of: (1) no disqualifying Health Care Worker Background Check without a waiver; (2) a copy of the Social Security card; (3) a visa or proof of citizenship that meets federal employment requirements.

citations.title: Initial training - home services agency
citations.requirement: The agency must provide or arrange at least 10 hours of initial training per worker. Five hours must come before the first assignment, and the other 5 within 30 days of the start of employment. The agency may accept proof of training from another licensed home services agency within the prior 365 days, including a CNA on the Health Care Worker Registry. Such workers still get a competency evaluation before their first assignment. No assignment may be given until the worker passes a competency evaluation on the first 5 hours of topics, with a second test after the remaining 5 hours. (The 8-hour figure in 245.71(b) and 245.214(e) applies only to placement agencies.)

citations.title: Required training subjects
citations.requirement: Training must cover, in addition to 245.40(c)(4)(A)-(P): job responsibilities and limits; communication with people who are hard of hearing or have dementia; observing, reporting and documenting; personal care tasks including medication reminding; adaptive equipment; hygiene and infection control; a clean and safe environment; safety precautions; emergencies, first aid and the client's emergency preparedness plan; confidentiality; understanding dementia; problem-solving for challenging dementia behaviors; abuse and neglect and reporting duties; and any other task the agency assigns.

citations.title: Annual training
citations.requirement: Every worker needs at least 10 hours of training per year of employment, on a calendar-year or anniversary basis chosen by the agency. The initial 10 hours satisfy the first year. Self-study with demonstrated learning is allowed. Annual training must include: client dignity, independence, self-determination, privacy, choice and rights; disaster procedures; hygiene and infection control; abuse and neglect prevention and reporting; and the ADL tasks in 245.40(c)(4)(A)-(P), including oxygen delivery for workers who serve clients on oxygen.

citations.title: Supervisors/trainers and training documentation
citations.requirement: The agency must have home services supervisors or trainers who give initial training and ongoing supervision. Each must either (1) have at least 2 years of qualifying experience within the last 5 years, or (2) hold a current supervisory or trainer position and have had training within the past year on the permitted tasks, provided by or developed by a qualified professional. Supervisors and trainers must be available to workers for continuing education. All training must be documented with date, minutes per topic, instructor and qualifications, content description, and worker signature or electronic certificate with date/time stamp.

citations.title: Health Care Worker Background Check
citations.requirement: An agency must comply with the Health Care Worker Background Check Act (225 ILCS 46) and the Health Care Worker Background Check Code (77 Ill. Adm. Code 955).

citations.title: Health Care Worker Background Check Act and Code
citations.requirement: Fingerprint-based checks are required for covered workers. Fingerprints are sent to the Illinois State Police within 10 working days (per the research). Results initiated through IDPH are entered in the Health Care Worker Registry. The application package requires proof of access to the IDPH Registry (955.115, per Form 445104).

citations.title: Infection Control
citations.requirement: Each agency must develop and implement policies and procedures for investigating, controlling and preventing infections. The requirement for placement agencies to give workers the CDC hand-hygiene guideline does not apply to a direct-service agency. Subsection (b), on adherence to CDC guidance, was only partly visible; read it in full.

citations.title: Vaccinations (scope)
citations.requirement: Influenza and pneumococcal vaccination duties apply to home health agencies and home nursing agencies, not to home services agencies. Do not write client vaccination procedures for this license.

citations.title: Services - Home Services Agencies: scope and contracted services
citations.requirement: A home services agency provides non-medical services, directly or by contract, such as ADL support, personal care, medication reminding, housekeeping, laundry, cooking, shopping, transport to appointments, household records and companionship. The agency must keep a list of services offered and the scope of work for each. It must give that list to clients before contracting, with the signed contract, and whenever it changes. Contracts with third-party providers must be written and include 9 elements: services, adherence to agency policies and personnel requirements, agency control, notes, charges, liability and insurance, term, signatures, and termination.

citations.title: Written client agreement
citations.requirement: A written client agreement must include: (1) assurance of compliance with the Act, including the Health Care Worker Background Check Act; (2) who pays employment taxes, Social Security taxes and workers' compensation; (3) who supervises workers and who hires, fires and disciplines them; (4) charges, payment schedule and payee; (5) contract term and termination conditions; (6) contact information for concerns, complaints and questions.

citations.title: Acceptance of clients; discharge
citations.requirement: The agency must develop and follow written acceptance and discharge policies. Acceptance is based on need for non-medical help, and the agency may not provide medical services. A totally dependent repositioning client may be accepted only if the worker is trained and competency-evaluated and the representative can assist or give feedback. No one may be refused service on the basis of the protected classes listed in 775 ILCS 5/1-103(Q). Termination requires at least 7 working days' written notice with a stated reason, kept in the record. The 7-day notice does not apply when worker safety is at risk, and the risk must be documented. Acceptance must be based on documented functional limitations and relevant circumstances, including basic information on medications, treatments, activity, diet and mental status.

citations.title: Service plan
citations.requirement: A plan is required for every client, developed with agency staff, the client or representative or POA, and family if the client wishes. It must cover ADL and in-home support, medication reminders (frequency and time of day), treatments being received, activity, diet, functional limitations and essential procedures, mental health status, frequency of visits, equipment, and client limitations. It may not include tasks outside the worker scope in 245.40(c)(4). No physician signature is required. Review and revise as needed, and at least annually.

citations.title: Client records, retention, confidentiality
citations.requirement: Each client record must hold identifying information, representative contact information, an emergency contact, the agreed service plan, the signed home care services agreement, and worker documentation of each service at each visit. A written records policy is required. Records must be kept at least 2 years after the last date of service, in hard copy or electronic form. Faxed copies must be on non-thermal paper. A written confidentiality policy must cover use, removal and release of records.

citations.title: Services - Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias
citations.requirement: The section exists per the table of contents. Its text was not retrieved. IDPH's FAQ points agencies to 77 Ill. Adm. Code 973 for dementia requirements. Read both before finalizing the dementia policy.

citations.title: Staff Training (Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Code)
citations.requirement: IDPH survey guidance names this section as the training standard for home services and home nursing agencies, together with 245.71. The rule text and dementia hour counts were not retrieved. A secondary source says 6 hours initial and 3 hours annual; treat that as unverified.

citations.title: Client Service Contracts - Home Nursing and Home Services Agencies
citations.requirement: The section title was confirmed from the table of contents. Its text was not retrieved. Use the 245.210(c) contract elements above, then read 245.220 in full for added contract terms.

citations.title: Quality Improvement Program
citations.requirement: Home nursing, home services and placement agencies must develop a quality improvement program with written policies. The program must evaluate the agency's total program at least once a year. Subsection (b) requires record review. Its detail, and the content of the evaluation for home services agencies, was not retrieved; read in full.

citations.title: Abuse, Neglect and Financial Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
citations.requirement: On reasonable suspicion of abuse, neglect or financial exploitation of a client aged 60+, a disabled client, or any 'eligible adult' under the Adult Protective Services Act (320 ILCS 20), notify the elder abuse provider agency designated by IDoA or the Area Agency on Aging. For a victim under 18, call the DCFS Child Abuse Hotline. Document each report and keep it on premises for 12 months. If an employee is the alleged perpetrator, remove them from direct client contact immediately and investigate. Complete a written investigation report within 14 days of the initial report. Send it to IDPH within 24 hours after the investigation is completed and keep a copy for 12 months. The report must contain the six elements in (d). Employees and volunteers must report to management and to the elder abuse provider agency or IDoA. Call 911 or local police immediately for staff-inflicted physical injury, sexual abuse by staff, a crime in the home by another person, or a death other than by disease or natural causes. A written law-enforcement notification policy is required. Mandated-reporter duties under 320 ILCS 20 remain.

citations.title: Services - Home Services Placement Agency
citations.requirement: A placement agency may not be the employer, may not direct or supervise the worker, and may charge only a one-time placement fee. It must identify itself as a placement agency in all marketing. This section does not apply to a direct-service (employer) agency; the manual should state which model the agency uses.

citations.title: License Application - evidence of liability insurance
citations.requirement: The agency must show evidence of liability insurance. The 245.30(b)(2) text confirms the cross-reference. The minimum limits were not confirmed; a secondary source says $1M per occurrence and $3M aggregate, which is unverified.

citations.title: Provisional License
citations.requirement: Provisional license valid 240 days, extendable 120 days with substantial progress. The full home services license expires one year from the end of the month the provisional license was first issued. (From the fact-checked research.)

citations.title: Adverse Licensure Actions - application not completed within 90 days
citations.requirement: An application not completed and approved within 90 days of submission may be denied (as cited by IDPH; from the research).

citations.title: Inspections and Investigations
citations.requirement: The section title was confirmed from the table of contents. Its text was not retrieved. Read it before writing the survey policy.

citations.title: Complaints
citations.requirement: The section title was confirmed from the table of contents. Its text was not retrieved. Read it before writing the IDPH-complaint procedure.

citations.title: Home Services Agencies Frequently Asked Questions
citations.requirement: Licensees take private pay or private insurance. Medicaid clients are served through IDoA CCP or DHS-DRS. IDPH does an initial application review within 30 days. A compliance survey takes place within 30 days of provisional license expiration. The agency needs IDPH approval before serving a new county. The agency must notify IDPH within 10 days of any change, using the Facility Information Change Form. (From the research.)

citations.cite: IDPH Guidance for Common Deficiency Findings
citations.title: Common Survey Deficiencies - annual registry verification and education
citations.requirement: Surveyors cite 245.71 (home services only) and 973.140 for training deficiencies. The guidance covers annual Health Care Worker Registry verification and annual education. Training records must show date, minutes per topic, instructor and qualifications, content and worker signature. This is survey guidance, not a rule.

citations.title: Home Services Application
citations.requirement: The application requires: complaint-resolution policy; employee health and safety policy; infection control policy; background-check process; supervisory-visit policies; employee training procedure (245.71); sample service plan; job descriptions; and proof of IDPH Registry access. A $1,500 fee by check or money order is due with the application. The form has an 'Alternate Agency Manager' line. (From the research.)

citations.cite: HFS Electronic Visit Verification; December 2025 Illinois EVV Updates
citations.title: Illinois EVV for Medicaid personal care
citations.requirement: Personal care and home health EVV data is integrated in HHAeXchange from March 2, 2026. HFS requires at least 75% quarterly EVV compliance from April 1, 2026. The state EVV solution is free to providers. (From the research.)

citations.cite: IDoA Community Care Program current rates (eff. 1/1/2026)
citations.title: CCP in-home service rate S5130
citations.requirement: CCP in-home service (S5130) is $30.80/hour statewide, or $32.57/hour with insurance. IDoA is the operating agency, and Care Coordination Units assess and refer clients. Senior HelpLine 1-800-252-8966 is for client applications. (From the research.)

citations.title: HSP maximum unit prices
citations.requirement: Homemaker (4100) $30.80/hour; personal assistant (4150) $20.00/hour; non-agency CNA (4198) $23.00/hour. HSP serves people with severe disabilities under age 60. (From the research.)

citations.cite: HFS Persons who are Elderly waiver
citations.title: Persons who are Elderly HCBS waiver
citations.requirement: HFS is the state Medicaid agency and IDoA is the operating agency for the Persons who are Elderly waiver. (From the research.)

citations.title: Illinois Minimum Wage Law
citations.requirement: State minimum wage law. Rates are from secondary sources and conflict for Chicago, so confirm with IDOL and the City of Chicago. Statute text was not retrieved. The URL is a placeholder; replace with the ilga.gov page for 820 ILCS 105.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Agency Manager Responsibilities
state_specifics: The governing body has legal authority. It needs bylaws or equivalent, reviewed annually. It adopts and revises policies, meets to review operations, and keeps minutes (245.30(a)).
Designate an agency manager to supervise the provision of services under 245.30(f)(1). The research's '245.40(f)' citation is unconfirmed; use 245.30(f)(1).
Manager duties are in 245.40(a)(1)-(13). They include keeping the Act and rules on file and familiarizing staff with them.
Maintain an organizational chart down to the client level (245.40(a)(6)).
Designate in writing a qualified person to act in the manager's absence (245.40(a)(11)). The IDPH application has an Alternate Agency Manager line.
No RN requirement applies to a home services agency. The RN-supervisor rules in 245.30(d)-(e) are for home health agencies.
No manager qualification list for home services was found in 245.30(f). Ask IDPH what documents it wants before naming the manager.

policies.title: Licensure, Service Area, Insurance and Advertising Requirements
state_specifics: An IDPH Home Services Agency license is required before operating. Do not accept clients before the provisional license is issued.
Programs that serve only through CCP, DRS or the VA are excluded from the definition (245.20). Any private-pay or mixed agency needs the license.

Application is Form 445104 with a $1,500 fee, by check or money order. Electronic submission and payment are not accepted. IDPH does an initial review within 30 days. An application not completed and approved within 90 days may be denied (245.130(b)). Provisional license is valid 240 days (extendable 120 days). A survey takes place within 30 days of its expiration. The full license runs one year from the end of the month of first issuance (245.100).
Renewal is due 60 days before expiration. The renewal fee has not been verified.
The manual must state the agency is a direct-service employer. Placement-agency rules (245.214: one-time fee, no direction or supervision of the worker, 'placement agency' labeling) do not apply.
Get IDPH approval before serving a new county. Notify IDPH within 10 days of any change (ownership, manager, address, phone) using the Facility Information Change Form.
Keep evidence of liability insurance current (245.30(b)(2), 245.90(a)). The $1M/$3M limits are unconfirmed.
Marketing should display the IDPH license status and list only approved counties.
IDPH Home Services Program: 217-782-7412, TTY 800-547-0466, DPH.COOS@illinois.gov.

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
state_specifics: The governing body reviews bylaws at least annually and adopts and revises policies as needed (245.30(a)(1), (3)). Record each review in the minutes (245.30(a)(5)).
The manager must keep the Department's rules on file and make them available to employees and contracted providers (245.40(a)(2)-(3)).
Written administrative policies must exist to ensure safe and adequate care (245.30(b)(1)).

Keep a version log. Keep the policies named in the Form 445104 package current: complaints, employee health and safety, infection control, background checks, supervisory visits, training, service plan, job descriptions.

policies.title: Quality Improvement Program
state_specifics: A written quality improvement program is required for home services agencies (245.240(a)).
It must evaluate the agency's total program at least once a year (245.240(a)).
245.240(b) requires record review. Its detail, and the other content requirements, were not retrieved; read 245.240 in full.
Review inputs: client records and service plans, supervisory-visit findings, complaints, incident and abuse investigations, training and competency results.
Report results to the governing body and record them in the minutes.

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
state_specifics: Part 245 has no compliance-program rule. The manager must ensure compliance with all applicable federal, State and local laws (245.40(a)(1)).
Bill only for services documented in the visit record. For CCP or HSP clients, bill only at the program's posted rate and only for EVV-verified visits.
CCP S5130 is $30.80/hour, or $32.57/hour with insurance (eff. 1/1/2026). HSP homemaker 4100 is $30.80/hour (updated 7/1/2026).
Exclusion screening, an audit schedule and a non-retaliation reporting channel are agency-set controls. No Illinois rule for them was fetched.

policies.title: Operating Hours, Office and After-Hours Access
state_specifics: Keep an office with a working telephone staffed during business hours (245.40(a)(12)).
The office must protect the confidentiality of paper and electronic records and meet local fire-safety rules (245.40(a)(12)(B)-(C)).
Adopt a written operating-hours policy. It must tell clients how to reach care from the agency or another provider outside those hours (245.40(a)(13)).
A supervisor must be reachable by workers at all times (245.40(c)(6)(A)).

policies.title: Contracted Services and Subcontractor Agreements
state_specifics: Contracts with third parties need a written agreement with the nine elements in 245.210(b): description of services; adherence to agency policies and personnel requirements; full agency control; notes; charges; liability and insurance for employment and workers' compensation taxes; term; signatures; termination.
Contracted personnel must hold any required license, registration or certification and be supervised by the agency (245.30(c)(5)).
Contracted workers must meet the same health evaluation and background check requirements as employees (245.210(b)(2)).

policies.title: IDPH Surveys, Inspections, Complaint Investigations and Plans of Correction
state_specifics: IDPH must survey on-site within 30 days of the provisional license expiring.
Name one person to receive IDPH contacts and respond the same day.
Sections 245.110 (inspections and investigations) and 245.115 (complaints) were not retrieved. Read them before finalizing this policy.
IDPH's common-deficiency guidance covers annual Registry verification and annual education. Run a mock survey about 60 days before the provisional license ends.
Keep a copy of every IDPH finding and the correction made.

policies.title: Client Rights and Responsibilities
state_specifics: The Part 245 sections fetched contain no standalone client bill of rights for home services agencies. Build the rights list from the required training topics and 245.210(d)(3).
Required training topics: dignity, independence, self-determination, privacy, choice and rights (245.71(f)(1)).
Clients may not be refused service on protected-class grounds (245.210(d)(3)). A client's representative or POA participates in the service plan (245.210(e)).
Give the client the termination terms and complaint contact information in the agreement (245.210(c)(5)-(6)).
For CCP and HSP clients, add the HCBS settings rights that apply under the waiver.

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: A written complaint-resolution policy covering the agency, its clients and client advocates is required (245.30(b)(3)). It is also in the IDPH application package.
Give each client contact information for concerns, complaints and questions in the written agreement (245.210(c)(6)).
Complaints to IDPH are governed by 245.115, which was not retrieved.
Keep a complaint log with dates, findings and responses. Feed it into the QI evaluation.

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: A written policy must explain the use, removal and release of client records (245.210(j)).
The office must protect the confidentiality of paper and electronic records (245.40(a)(12)(B)).
Workers are trained on confidentiality of client personal, financial and health information (245.71(e)(10)).
Personnel record confidentiality is also required (245.30(c)(1)(G)).
HIPAA applies if the agency bills electronically for Medicaid-funded services or otherwise qualifies as a covered entity. Confirm the status with counsel.

policies.title: Client Property, Gifts and Financial Exploitation Prevention
state_specifics: Financial exploitation is a reportable event under 245.250(a). Report within the same channel as abuse and neglect.
Workers are trained on behaviors that constitute abuse and neglect (245.71(e)(13)).
Shopping and household-records tasks (245.210(a)) require receipts and a reconciliation record. Set a written rule for gifts, loans, wills and use of client funds or cards.
Immediately remove any worker accused of exploitation from direct client contact and investigate (245.250(a)(3)).

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
federal: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act (42 USC 2000d)
state_specifics: No person may be refused service because of actual or perceived race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, age, sex, marital status, order of protection status, disability, military status, sexual orientation, pregnancy or unfavorable military discharge (245.210(d)(3), citing 775 ILCS 5/1-103(Q)).
Personnel policies must cover Civil Rights Act of 1964 compliance (245.30(c)(1)(F)).
Train workers in communication with people who are hard of hearing or have dementia (245.71(e)(2)).
Interpreter and translation procedures are agency-set. No Part 245 provision on them was fetched.

policies.title: Service Agreement, Rates and Billing Disclosure
state_specifics: Give the client the list of services offered and the scope of work for each before contracting, with the signed contract, and whenever the list changes (245.210(a)).

The written agreement must include the six items in 245.210(c): compliance assurance; who pays employment taxes and workers' compensation; who supervises, hires, fires and disciplines workers; charges and payment schedule and payee; term and termination; complaint contact.
Section 245.220 (client service contracts) was not retrieved. Read it for additional contract terms.
For CCP or HSP clients the program rate governs. Do not bill the client for the difference unless the program permits it.

policies.title: Scope of Services - What Home Services Workers May and May Not Do
state_specifics: Home services are non-medical. They exclude anything requiring a Nurse Practice Act licensee (245.40(c)(1)). The agency may not provide services a home health or home nursing agency would provide (245.210(d)(1)).
Permitted duties include observing and reporting, chores, shopping, appointments, companionship, documentation, and ADL and personal care (245.40(c)(3)).

Prohibited or limited: skilled skin care, wound care, dressing changes, tube or syringe feeding, nail trimming, passive range of motion, catheter insertion or removal, and medication setup (245.40(c)(4)-(5)).
The service plan may not include out-of-scope tasks (245.210(e)(4)).
If a client's needs become skilled, refer to a home health or home nursing agency.

policies.title: Client Intake, Acceptance and Assessment
state_specifics: Written acceptance policies are required (245.210(d)). Acceptance is based on the client's desire or need for household, personal support or companionship help.

Document, in consultation with the client and family or representative: functional limitations and their relevance to the services requested; and basic information on medications, treatments, activity, diet and mental status (245.210(d)(5)).

A client who needs complete repositioning with no ability to signal may be accepted only if the worker is trained, the representative can assist or give feedback, and the agency has evaluated worker competency (245.210(d)(2)).
No one may be refused for protected-class reasons (245.210(d)(3)).

policies.title: Service Plan and Plan Updates
state_specifics: Develop a plan for each client with staff, the client or representative or POA, and family if the client wishes (245.210(e)).

Required content: ADL and in-home support; medication reminders (frequency and time); treatments received; activity; diet; functional limitations and essential procedures; mental health status; frequency of visits; equipment; client limitations.
No physician signature is required (245.210(f)).
Review and revise as needed, and at least annually (245.210(g)).
The plan is part of the client record (245.210(h)(4)).

policies.title: Supervision of Home Services Workers and Supervisory Visits
state_specifics: Designate a supervisor who is available to workers for questions at all times (245.40(c)(6)(A)).
Make an on-site visit to observe the worker giving care when an area of concern is noted, no later than the next supervisory visit.
Make an annual on-site visit to observe and assess each worker giving care.
The interval for routine supervisory visits must be confirmed in 245.40(c)(6)(B) (a secondary source says every 90 days; not verified). The visit-form content must also be confirmed there.
Supervisors and trainers must meet the experience or training qualifications in 245.71(g) and be available for continuing education (245.71(h)).
A supervisory-visit policy is part of the IDPH application package.

policies.title: Medication Reminding (No Medication Setup)
state_specifics: Workers may remind clients about medications only when the medications were pre-selected by the client, a family member, a nurse or a pharmacist and are stored in containers other than prescription bottles, such as medication minders.
Workers may not perform or provide medication setup. They may not administer, open or pour medications.
The service plan states the reminder frequency and time of day (245.210(e)(1)(B)).
Medication reminding is a required initial-training task (245.71(e)(4)).
Report missed doses, refusals or reactions to the supervisor and the client's emergency contact.

policies.title: Scheduling, Missed Visits and Continuity of Care
state_specifics: Visit frequency is set in the service plan (245.210(e)(1)(H)).
Each service at each visit must be documented by the worker (245.210(h)(6)).
Part 245 sets no staffing ratio, visit minimum or missed-visit rule for home services agencies in the sections fetched. Set the notification and replacement procedure as agency policy.
The operating-hours policy must tell clients how to reach care outside business hours (245.40(a)(13)).

policies.title: Electronic Visit Verification and Timekeeping
state_specifics: EVV applies only to Medicaid-funded personal care (CCP or HSP). Private-pay visits are outside the state EVV mandate.

Personal care and home health EVV data is integrated in HHAeXchange from March 2, 2026. At least 75% quarterly EVV compliance is required from April 1, 2026. The state EVV solution is offered at no cost.
A vendor summary lists the elements as caregiver, member, service, time in, time out and GPS location. Confirm against HFS documents.
Worker documentation of each visit is still required in the client record (245.210(h)(6)).
Review EVV exceptions weekly. Claims without a matching EVV visit may deny.

policies.title: Change in Client Condition and Emergencies in the Home
state_specifics: Workers observe client functioning and report changes to the supervisor, employer or a person the client designates (245.40(c)(3)(A)).
Workers are trained to recognize emergencies and start emergency procedures, including basic first aid and the client's emergency preparedness plan (245.71(e)(9)).
Each record has an emergency contact (245.210(h)(3)). Open skin lesions found during shampooing must be reported to the agency and the emergency contact (245.40(c)(4)(G)(iii)).
Call 911 and local law enforcement for a crime in the home or a death other than by natural causes (245.250(f)).
Document the event and the supervisor's follow-up in the client record.

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Discontinuation of Services
state_specifics: A written discharge policy is required (245.210(d)).
The agency must give the client at least 7 working days' notice with a stated reason before terminating services, and keep it in the client record (245.210(d)(4)).
The 7-day notice does not apply when worker safety is at risk. Document the risk in the record.
If the client's needs become medical, refer them to a home health or home nursing agency (245.210(d)(1)).
The agreement must state termination conditions (245.210(c)(5)).

policies.title: Coordination with Medicaid Programs (CCP, HSP) and Payers
state_specifics: Medicaid clients reach a licensed home services agency through IDoA CCP (via Care Coordination Units) or DHS-DRS Home Services Program. IDoA is the operating agency for the Persons who are Elderly waiver and HFS is the state Medicaid agency.
CCP in-home service S5130 is $30.80/hour, or $32.57/hour with insurance (eff. 1/1/2026).
HSP maximum unit prices (updated 7/1/2026): homemaker 4100 $30.80/hour; personal assistant 4150 $20.00/hour; non-agency CNA 4198 $23.00/hour. HSP serves people with severe disabilities under 60.
CCP provider enrollment steps were not confirmed. Confirm with IDoA, and with DRS whether a new agency can bill HSP at agency rates.
Senior HelpLine 1-800-252-8966 handles client applications, not provider enrollment.

policies.title: Task-Specific Conditions and Competency Evaluations (Bathing, Positioning, Feeding, Nail Care and Other Tasks)
state_specifics: Most tasks require three conditions: the client or representative can give ongoing feedback; the worker is trained in the method; and the agency has done a competency evaluation (245.40(c)(4)).
Bathing needs client-specific training and competency, plus annual training and competency for all bathing types (245.40(c)(4)(C)). Prescription shampoo needs an order and annual training (G).
Nail filing for clients with circulatory or sensation problems needs a health care professional's order (I). Prescription compression devices need an order (D).
Thickener may be opened pre-measured under direct client observation with training and competency (F).
Feeding: the client must be able to swallow independently and be upright. High choking risk means a home health or home nursing agency must serve (F).
Positioning for clients who cannot signal for a change needs training and competency (J) and is limited by 245.210(d)(2).

Oxygen delivery support applies only to workers assigned to such clients. An agency that has workers change stationary-to-portable oxygen must keep a trained on-staff individual who can train and test (245.40(c)(4)(P) and related text; read in full).
Training and the competency check must be documented (245.71(i)).

policies.title: Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Services
state_specifics: Dementia content is required in initial training: understanding dementia and problem-solving for challenging behavior (245.71(e)(11)-(12)).

77 Ill. Adm. Code 973 and 245.211 apply to agencies that serve clients with dementia. Their text was not retrieved. Confirm the hour counts and policy content before publishing; do not state dementia hour counts as verified.
IDPH survey guidance cites 973.140 for training compliance (home services and home nursing).
Include in the service plan the client's behaviors, triggers and safety needs, drawn from the intake assessment.

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Report reasonable suspicion of abuse, neglect or financial exploitation of a client who is 60+, disabled or an eligible adult under the Adult Protective Services Act (320 ILCS 20) to the elder abuse provider agency designated by IDoA or the Area Agency on Aging for the client's area.
For a victim under 18, notify DCFS through the Child Abuse Hotline.
Document each report and keep it on premises for 12 months.
Employees and volunteers must report to agency management and to the elder abuse provider agency or IDoA (245.250(e)). Mandated-reporter duties under 320 ILCS 20 are unchanged.
Train every worker at hire and annually on prevention and reporting (245.71(e)(13), (f)(4)).
Hotline numbers (IDoA Adult Protective Services, DCFS) were not retrieved; confirm current numbers before printing them on cards.

policies.title: Incident Reporting
state_specifics: Part 245 has no separate incident-reporting rule. The reportable categories in 245.250 are abuse, neglect, financial exploitation, staff-inflicted injury, sexual abuse, crime in the home, and death other than by disease or natural causes.
Define internal incident types (falls, injuries, property loss, medication reminding errors, worker injury) and a reporting deadline as agency policy.
File each incident report in the client record or an incident log, with supervisor follow-up.
Route suspected abuse and neglect events to SAF-01, SAF-07 and SAF-08.

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
federal: 29 CFR 1910.1030 (only where tasks create occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious materials)
state_specifics: Written policies and procedures for investigating, controlling and preventing infections are required (245.75(a)). An infection control policy is part of the IDPH application package.
Workers are trained on hygiene and infection control at hire and annually (245.71(e)(6), (f)(3)).
Employee health policy: employees report symptoms and exposure to communicable disease, with set conditions for removal from and return to client contact (245.30(c)(1)(H)).
The influenza and pneumococcal vaccination duties in 245.55 apply to home health and home nursing agencies, not to home services agencies.
Perform an OSHA exposure determination for tasks such as pericare, catheter bags and ostomy bags.

policies.title: Client Emergency and Disaster Plans
state_specifics: Workers are trained to implement the client's emergency preparedness plan (245.71(e)(9)) and on disaster procedures at hire and annually (245.71(f)(2)).
Each record needs an emergency contact (245.210(h)(3)).
The Part 245 sections fetched contain no agency-wide emergency preparedness plan rule for home services agencies. The federal emergency preparedness rule for home health agencies does not apply.
Write a per-client emergency plan at intake covering evacuation ability, medical equipment, power-dependent devices and who to call.
Adopt a continuity plan for severe weather and staff shortages.

policies.title: Caregiver Safety in the Home and Workplace Violence
state_specifics: Written agency procedures for identifying potential dangers to workers in the home and protecting them are required (245.30(c)(1)(I)). An employee health and safety policy is part of the application package.
Workers are trained on basic personal and environmental safety precautions (245.71(e)(8)).
A worker may leave and report an unsafe home. Document the risk, since the 7-working-day termination notice does not apply when worker safety is at risk (245.210(d)(4)).
Do a safety check at intake. Cover pets, firearms, smoking, bed bugs and unsafe conditions.

policies.title: Transporting Clients
state_specifics: Assistance in getting to and from appointments and shopping is a permitted service (245.210(a), 245.40(c)(3)(C)).
The sections fetched contain no transport-specific standards. Set agency policy on: driver license verification, vehicle insurance, passenger consent, seat belt use and mobility device securement.
Liability insurance evidence is required for licensing (245.30(b)(2), 245.90(a)). Confirm with the carrier that client transport, and hired and non-owned auto use, are covered.

policies.title: Law Enforcement Notification and Crime in the Client's Home
state_specifics: Contact local law enforcement immediately (for example, 911) for: physical abuse causing injury by a staff member; sexual abuse by a staff member; a crime in the client's home by another person; a death other than by disease processes; or any reported allegation of physical abuse, sexual abuse or crime (245.250(f)).

The written policy must cover: client safety in these situations; contacting police, fire, ambulance and rescue; contacting police when someone abuses a client physically; and seeking advice on preserving a potential crime scene (245.250(g)).
Notifying police does not replace reporting to the elder abuse provider agency (245.250(h)).

policies.title: Investigation of Allegations Against Employees and 14-Day Written Report
state_specifics: If an employee is the alleged abuser, immediately remove the person from direct client contact and investigate (245.250(a)(3)).
Complete a written report of findings within 14 days after the initial report (245.250(b)).
Send the written report to IDPH within 24 hours after the investigation is completed. Keep a copy on agency premises for 12 months.

The report must include: dates, times and description; description of injury or abuse; actions taken by the licensee; individuals and agencies interviewed or notified; action to prevent recurrence; and witness statements (245.250(d)).

policies.title: Home Services Worker Qualifications and Health Care Worker Registry
state_specifics: For each worker who is not otherwise licensed, certified or registered, keep in the employee file: no disqualifying background check without a waiver; a copy of the Social Security card; and proof of citizenship or work authorization (245.71(a)).
A CNA on the Health Care Worker Registry may use prior training in place of initial training, but still gets a competency evaluation before the first assignment (245.71(c)).
Before employing someone in a position that requires a State professional license, verify with IDFPR that it is active and keep a copy (245.30(c)(2)).
The 245.70 home health aide training standard does not apply, because the agency does not offer home health aide services.
IDPH survey guidance covers annual Registry verification.

policies.title: Background Checks and Health Care Worker Registry
state_specifics: Comply with the Health Care Worker Background Check Act (225 ILCS 46) and Code 955 (245.72).
Fingerprint-based checks are sent to the Illinois State Police within 10 working days (per the research). Results initiated through IDPH are entered in the Health Care Worker Registry.
The application package requires a background check process and proof of Registry access (955.115).

Run the check and Registry steps for every new caregiver before the first assignment. Keep the results in the personnel file. Check Code 955 for how long results stay valid and for the waiver process.
IDPH survey guidance lists annual Registry verification as a common deficiency area.

policies.title: Orientation, Competency Evaluation and Annual Training
state_specifics: Initial training: at least 10 hours. Five hours before the first assignment, and the remaining 5 within 30 days of the start of employment (245.71(c)).
The worker may not get an assignment until passing a competency evaluation on the first 5 hours. A second test follows the remaining 5 hours.
Proof of training at another licensed home services agency within the prior 365 days (including a Registry-approved CNA) may substitute, with a competency evaluation first.
Initial content covers the 14 subjects in 245.71(e) plus 245.40(c)(4)(A)-(P).

Annual: at least 10 hours per year of employment (calendar or anniversary basis, chosen by the agency). The initial 10 hours satisfy year one. Required topics: rights, disaster procedures, infection control, abuse and neglect, and ADL tasks (245.71(f)).
Document date, minutes per topic, instructor and qualifications, content, and worker signature or time-stamped electronic completion (245.71(i)).
Placement-agency training (8 hours, 245.71(b)) is not the standard for a direct-service agency.

policies.title: Employee Health Evaluation and Communicable Disease Reporting
state_specifics: Part 245 requires an initial health evaluation of each new employee who has client contact, as specified by the governing body (245.30(c)(1)(B)).

Employee health policies must require employees to report symptoms and exposure to communicable disease. They must set the conditions for removal from client contact and for returning (245.30(c)(1)(H)).
No TB-specific test or schedule was found in the Part 245 sections fetched. The governing body must define what the evaluation includes. Confirm with IDPH before adopting a TB testing requirement.
Keep results in a confidential employee health file separate from the personnel file.

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Each personnel record includes: name and address; SSN; date of birth; next of kin; evidence of qualifications (license, registration or certification); employment dates; and separation date and reason (245.30(c)(3)).

Also keep: background check result, SSN card copy, proof of work authorization (245.71(a)); training and competency records (245.71(i)); IDFPR license verification where applicable (245.30(c)(2)); annual performance evaluation (245.30(c)(1)(E)).
Personnel records must be kept confidential (245.30(c)(1)(G)).
The Part 245 sections fetched set no personnel-record retention period. Set one and confirm it with counsel.

policies.title: Wage, Hour and Overtime Compliance
state_specifics: Personnel policies must cover wage scales, benefits, hours of work and leave (245.30(c)(1)(A)).
Third-party employers such as a licensed agency cannot claim the companionship or live-in exemptions; pay overtime for hours over 40 per week (29 CFR 552).
Pay for travel between clients as hours worked.
State minimum wage is $15.00/hour per secondary sources. Cook County and Chicago rates are higher and step up each July 1. The sources conflict for Chicago; confirm with IDOL and the City of Chicago.
Illinois Paid Leave for All Workers Act applies per the research summary. Confirm current text and any local ordinance with counsel.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Workers are trained on job responsibilities and limitations (245.71(e)(1)).
Conduct that is abuse, neglect or financial exploitation is reportable and triggers immediate removal from client contact (245.250(a)(3)).
Policy topics: gifts and tips, personal relationships, social media, client money, personal use of client property, and working outside agency scope.
Personnel policies must cover Civil Rights Act compliance (245.30(c)(1)(F)).

policies.title: Job Descriptions, Performance Evaluations and Hiring Authority
state_specifics: Job descriptions are required for all positions the agency uses (245.30(c)(1)(D)). They are part of the IDPH application package.
An annual performance evaluation is required for all employees (245.30(c)(1)(E)).
The manager hires qualified personnel according to job descriptions (245.40(a)(9)).
The agreement tells clients who hires, fires and disciplines workers (245.210(c)(3)).

policies.title: Home Services Supervisor and Trainer Qualifications
state_specifics: Every supervisor or trainer needs one of two qualifications. Either (1) at least 2 years of experience within the last 5 years in home health, home services, facility-based healthcare or home nursing performing worker-permitted tasks, including ADL help; or (2) a current supervisory or trainer position with a home services agency plus training within the past year on the permitted tasks (245.71(g)).

For option (2), the training must show the general standards of care for each topic in 245.40(c)(4)(A)-(P). It must be provided or developed by someone qualified (for example, licensed or certified) in that field.
Keep proof of qualifications in the supervisor's personnel file.

policies.title: Contracted and Subcontracted Staff Verification
state_specifics: Contracted staff must hold any current license, registration or certification required by State or federal law and work under agency supervision (245.30(c)(5)).

The written third-party agreement must provide for adherence to agency policies and personnel requirements, including health evaluations, employee health policies and criminal background checks (245.210(b)(2)).
Verify active IDFPR licenses before use (245.30(c)(2)).
Contract workers get the same training, competency and Registry steps as employees.

policies.title: Client Records and Retention
state_specifics: Each client record has: identifying information; representative's contact information; emergency contact; plan of services; copy of the home care services agreement; and worker documentation of each service at each visit (245.210(h)).
Retain records at least 2 years after the last date of service, in paper or electronic form (245.210(i)).
Faxed copies must be on non-thermal paper, and the originals kept 2 years by the originating entity (245.210(i)).
A written records policy is required (245.210(i)).
Abuse and neglect reports and investigation reports must be kept on premises for 12 months (245.250).
HIPAA documentation retention is 6 years. CCP and HSP manuals may set longer periods; confirm with IDoA and DRS.

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Abuse, neglect or exploitation: report to the elder abuse provider agency designated by IDoA or the Area Agency on Aging, or to DCFS for a victim under 18 (245.250(a)).
Employee-perpetrator investigations: written report to IDPH within 24 hours after the investigation is completed, and within 14 days of the initial report (245.250(b)).
Changes: notify IDPH within 10 days using the Facility Information Change Form.
New county: written IDPH approval before serving clients there.
Renewal: file before the full license expires (one year from the end of the month of first provisional issuance). The application is due 60 days before expiration. Confirm the current fee.
Keep the IDPH license posted or on file and insurance evidence current.

policies.title: Release, Removal and Confidentiality of Client Records
state_specifics: A written policy must explain the use, removal and release of records (245.210(j)).
The office must be maintained to protect confidentiality of physical and electronic records (245.40(a)(12)(B)).

Set rules on who may remove records from the office, such as for supervisory visits. Require a signed authorization for release, except where law allows disclosure (for example, abuse reporting under 245.250).
Honor a client's request for access to their record under HIPAA, within 30 days.

forms.name: Home Services Client Agreement
forms.purpose: Written contract with the six elements of 245.210(c): compliance assurance, tax and workers' compensation responsibility, supervision and hiring, charges and payee, term and termination, complaint contact.

forms.name: Schedule of Services and Scope of Work
forms.purpose: List of services offered with scope for each, given to the client before contracting, with the signed agreement, and on any change.

forms.name: Client Intake and Acceptance Assessment
forms.purpose: Documents functional limitations, medications, treatments, activity, diet, mental status and acceptance decision.

forms.name: Home Safety and Emergency Preparedness Assessment
forms.purpose: Home hazards for worker safety and the client's emergency plan.

forms.name: Service Plan
forms.purpose: Plan with all 245.210(e) elements, reviewed at least annually.

forms.name: Worker Visit Documentation / Timesheet
forms.purpose: Documents each service at each visit; also feeds payroll and EVV.

forms.name: Medication Reminder Log
forms.purpose: Records reminders given from pre-set medication minders; no setup.

forms.name: Task-Specific Competency Checklists
forms.purpose: Competency evaluations for bathing, positioning, feeding thickener, nail care, prescription shampoo, compression devices and oxygen tasks.

forms.name: Supervisory Visit Report
forms.purpose: Documents routine and annual on-site observation of each worker and follow-up on areas of concern.

forms.name: Training Record and Attendance Log
forms.purpose: Date, minutes per topic, instructor and qualifications, content and worker signature.

forms.name: Worker Competency Evaluation (initial 5 hours and remaining 5 hours)
forms.purpose: Documents pass results before first assignment and after the full 10 hours.

forms.name: Personnel File Checklist
forms.purpose: Checks every 245.30(c)(3) and 245.71(a) item is in the file.

forms.name: Background Check and Registry Verification Tracker
forms.purpose: Fingerprint submission dates, results, waivers, annual Registry verification.

forms.name: New Employee Health Evaluation and Symptom/Exposure Report
forms.purpose: Initial health evaluation and communicable disease reporting with return-to-work conditions.

forms.name: Incident Report
forms.purpose: Internal record of falls, injuries, property loss and worker injuries with supervisor follow-up.

forms.name: Abuse/Neglect/Exploitation Report Log
forms.purpose: Records reports to the elder abuse provider agency or DCFS; kept 12 months.

forms.name: Employee Allegation Investigation Report
forms.purpose: 14-day written report with the six 245.250(d) elements; sent to IDPH within 24 hours of completion.

forms.name: Law Enforcement Notification Log
forms.purpose: Documents 911 and police contacts under 245.250(f)-(g).

forms.name: Client Complaint/Grievance Form and Log
forms.purpose: Intake, investigation and resolution of complaints.

forms.name: Notice of Discontinuation of Services
forms.purpose: At least 7 working days' notice with stated reason, or documented safety exception.

forms.name: Third-Party Services Agreement
forms.purpose: Nine-element contract for contracted services.

forms.name: Governing Body Meeting Minutes and Annual Bylaws Review
forms.purpose: Evidence of annual bylaws review, policy adoption and operations review.

forms.name: Alternate Agency Manager Designation
forms.purpose: Written designation of the person who acts in the manager's absence.

forms.name: Annual Quality Improvement Evaluation
forms.purpose: Annual written evaluation of the agency's total program.

forms.name: IDPH Facility Information Change Form (tracking sheet)
forms.purpose: Tracks the 10-day change notice and new-county approval requests.
